title: Wabeno Economic Development Act
official_title: To provide for the conveyance of certain Federal land in Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Tiffany (R-WI); passed the House and was ordered reported favorably by the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. Single-parcel land conveyances at market value are usually low-controversy and clear the Senate when floor time allows.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended

summary: Directs the Forest Service to sell about 14 acres of national forest land in Wisconsin to a local company at market value, and orders a federal review of stone, sand, and gravel permitting.
brief: Conveys about 14 acres of Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest to a Wisconsin company at market value, plus a permitting review.

top_lines.headline: National Forest Land Sale
subs: About 14 acres in Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest
Sold to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC at appraised market value
Buyer pays survey, appraisal, and environmental costs

top_lines.headline: Permitting Review
subs: Interior review of stone, sand, and gravel permitting on federal land

items.main: Names the Act the “Wabeno Economic Development Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Conveyance of Certain National Forest System Land

items.main: Directs the Forest Service to convey about 14 acres of national forest land to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC at market value.
items.detail: If the company offers market value (set by a required appraisal) within 180 days of the appraisal's approval, the Secretary of Agriculture must convey the roughly 14-acre parcel in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest in Wisconsin, including mineral rights, by quitclaim deed within 180 days. The buyer pays the purchase price plus survey, appraisal, and environmental-analysis costs. For hazardous materials, the Secretary need only meet disclosure requirements, not remediate.

sections.label: Section 3 — Comprehensive Review of Federal Permitting Processes for Stone, Sand, and Gravel Development

items.main: Requires an Interior Department review of federal permitting for stone, sand, and gravel development on federal lands.
items.detail: Within 180 days, the Secretary of the Interior must report to the House Natural Resources and Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committees (and publish online) on the current permitting process and timelines, inefficiencies and duplicative steps, recommendations to streamline, and the economic impact of current timelines.

gaps: The bill conveys the parcel including mineral rights but does not restrict how the land may be used after sale.
It limits the government's hazardous-materials duty to disclosure, not cleanup, but does not address liability for contamination found later.

added: Conveyance of about 14 acres of Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest land to a private company at market value
Interior review and report on federal stone, sand, and gravel permitting

removed: Struck the Hazardous Materials carve-out (subsection (e)) that had limited the Secretary to only CERCLA section 120(h) disclosure and exempted any duty to remediate or abate disclosed contaminants — full CERCLA cleanup obligations now apply
